name: Thyroid gland
func: A butterfly-shaped gland in the front of the neck. It makes thyroid hormones that set how fast your body burns energy, and they matter for growth, brain development, heart rate and body temperature.

levels.kid:
The **thyroid** is a gland shaped like a **butterfly**, sitting in the front of your neck just below the bump in your throat.

It works like the **speed dial** for your body. It makes hormones that tell your body how fast to use energy, kind of like a gas pedal in a car.

If the thyroid makes too little, a person feels tired, slow and cold. If it makes too much, a person feels jumpy, hot and hungry, and their heart races.

To do its job, the thyroid needs **iodine**, which comes from food, like salt with iodine added and fish.
levels.hs:
The **thyroid gland** sits in the front of the neck at the level of the **C5–T1** vertebrae. It has two **lobes**, one on each side of the **trachea** (windpipe) and **larynx**, joined across the front of the 2nd to 4th tracheal rings by a narrow bridge called the **isthmus**. It lies below the thyroid cartilage (Adam's apple) and is covered by thin neck muscles. Behind it run the **carotid arteries**, and in the groove between the trachea and esophagus run the **recurrent laryngeal nerves**, which control the voice box. Tiny **parathyroid glands**, usually four, sit on its back surface.

The thyroid is made of thousands of hollow balls called **follicles**, filled with a protein gel called **colloid**. Follicle cells trap **iodine** from the blood and use it to make two hormones: **thyroxine (T4)** and **triiodothyronine (T3)**. T3 is the active form, and most of it is made by converting T4 in the body's tissues.

These hormones raise the **metabolic rate**, increase heat production, speed up the heart and are essential for normal **brain development** and growth in children.

The pituitary controls the thyroid with **TSH**, and thyroid hormones feed back to switch TSH down. Separate **C cells** (parafollicular cells) make **calcitonin**, which can lower blood calcium.
levels.college:
**Development**: the thyroid starts at the **foramen cecum** at the back of the tongue and descends through the neck as the **thyroglossal duct**, passing in front of the hyoid bone. Remnants can form a **thyroglossal duct cyst**, a midline lump that moves up when the tongue sticks out. A **pyramidal lobe** projecting up from the isthmus is a common remnant. Failure to descend leaves a **lingual thyroid**.

**Blood supply**: the **superior thyroid artery** (first branch of the external carotid) travels with the **external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve**, and the **inferior thyroid artery** (from the **thyrocervical trunk** of the subclavian) crosses the **recurrent laryngeal nerve** near the lower pole. An inconstant **thyroid ima artery** may rise from the brachiocephalic trunk or aortic arch. Veins: superior, middle and inferior thyroid veins.

The gland lies within the **pretracheal fascia**, so it moves up with swallowing, an important exam finding.

**Hormone synthesis**: follicular cells take up iodide with the **sodium–iodide symporter (NIS)**, move it into colloid through **pendrin**, then **thyroid peroxidase (TPO)** oxidizes it and attaches it to tyrosines on **thyroglobulin** (organification), and couples them into T3 and T4. The cell takes colloid back in by endocytosis, and lysosomes release the hormones. About 99% of circulating hormone is bound to proteins such as **thyroxine-binding globulin**; only the free fraction is active.

**Deiodinases** convert T4 to active T3 (D1, D2) or inactivate it (D3).
levels.phd:
Thyroid hormone acts mainly through nuclear **thyroid hormone receptors** (**TRα** and **TRβ**), which bind DNA at **thyroid response elements** as heterodimers with retinoid X receptors. Without hormone, TRs recruit **corepressors** (NCoR, SMRT) and histone deacetylases; T3 binding swaps them for **coactivators**, switching on genes. Receptor isoforms are tissue-specific: TRα dominates in heart and bone, while TRβ2 in the pituitary and hypothalamus mediates negative feedback on TSH and TRH.

Hormones enter cells through specific transporters, especially **MCT8** (SLC16A2). Mutations in MCT8 cause **Allan–Herndon–Dudley syndrome**: severe neurological impairment because T3 cannot reach brain neurons, despite high circulating T3. **Type 2 deiodinase** in astrocytes and tanycytes produces local T3 for the brain, so brain T3 levels can be held steady even when blood levels vary.

T3 increases metabolic rate partly by raising **Na+/K+-ATPase** activity, stimulating mitochondrial biogenesis and enhancing **futile cycles** that release heat, and in the heart by increasing **SERCA2** and alpha-myosin heavy chain while lowering phospholamban, making the heart beat faster and relax quicker.

The **Wolff–Chaikoff effect** is an autoregulatory drop in organification when iodide is very high, with escape after a few days through downregulation of NIS. Graves disease is caused by **TSH receptor–stimulating antibodies**, and Hashimoto thyroiditis involves T-cell destruction with antibodies to TPO and thyroglobulin.

Thyroid cancers have clear genetic drivers: **BRAF V600E** in papillary carcinoma, **RAS** mutations in follicular tumors, **RET** fusions in papillary cancer and germline **RET** mutations in **medullary carcinoma** (from C cells, part of MEN2).
levels.expert:
**Exam**: inspect and palpate from behind; a thyroid lump **moves up with swallowing**, while a thyroglossal cyst also moves with tongue protrusion. Check for lymph nodes and signs of thyroid dysfunction.

**Hypothyroidism** (most often **Hashimoto thyroiditis** in iodine-sufficient countries): fatigue, cold intolerance, weight gain, constipation, dry skin, slow relaxing reflexes and bradycardia. **High TSH** with low free T4. **Congenital hypothyroidism** is screened at birth because untreated it harms brain development. Treated with thyroid hormone replacement.

**Hyperthyroidism**, most commonly **Graves disease**: heat intolerance, weight loss, tremor, palpitations, **atrial fibrillation**, a diffuse goiter with a bruit, and Graves **eye disease** (proptosis, lid retraction) and pretibial myxedema. **Low TSH** with high free T4 or T3. Treatments include **antithyroid drugs**, **radioactive iodine** or surgery. **Thyroid storm** is a life-threatening emergency.

**Thyroid nodules** are very common. Workup: TSH, then **ultrasound** risk scoring (such as **TI-RADS**) and **fine-needle aspiration**, reported with the **Bethesda** system. **Papillary carcinoma** is the most common cancer and has an excellent prognosis. **Anaplastic carcinoma** is rare and very aggressive.

**Thyroidectomy** risks: injury to the **recurrent laryngeal nerve** (hoarse voice; bilateral injury can block the airway), the **external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve** (loss of high-pitched voice), and the **parathyroid glands** (low calcium, with tingling and **Chvostek** and **Trousseau** signs). Surgeons often use nerve monitoring. A rapidly expanding neck **hematoma** after surgery can compress the airway and must be opened immediately.

keyPoints: Butterfly-shaped gland: two lobes beside the trachea joined by the isthmus over rings 2–4
Follicles make T4 and T3 from iodine; C cells make calcitonin
Controlled by pituitary TSH with negative feedback
Recurrent laryngeal nerves and parathyroids lie behind it: key surgical risks
High TSH = hypothyroid; low TSH = hyperthyroid (most often Graves)

test.q: The thyroid isthmus lies in front of which tracheal rings?
test.explain: The isthmus crosses the 2nd to 4th tracheal rings.

test.q: The more active thyroid hormone, mostly made from T4 in tissues, is ______.
test.explain: Deiodinases remove one iodine from T4 to make T3.

test.q: Hoarseness after thyroid surgery suggests injury to the:
test.explain: The recurrent laryngeal nerve runs in the tracheoesophageal groove and supplies most larynx muscles.

test.q: A patient with high TSH and low free T4 most likely has:
test.explain: The failing gland makes too little hormone, so the pituitary raises TSH.

test.q: A midline neck cyst that moves up when the tongue is stuck out is a ______ duct cyst.
test.explain: It is a remnant of the thyroid's descent from the foramen cecum of the tongue.
